cases.question: What is PaymentOps Workbench?
cases.answer: PaymentOps Workbench is a personal project Nitin designed and built independently in 2026. It is a local-first, synthetic-data-only workbench for investigating payment exceptions and evaluating AI-assisted review behavior before promotion [project-paymentops#1]. It uses Python, Java and TypeScript across three services (React, Spring Boot, FastAPI) [project-paymentops#1]. cases.question: What is Ask Nitin and how is it built?
cases.answer:
Ask Nitin is the AI assistant on Nitin's portfolio website, a personal project from 2026. Recruiters can ask questions about his experience and get short answers with citations to his résumé, portfolio and project materials, or paste a job description to get a fit report that checks each requirement against those sources [project-ask-nitin#1].

Chat answers use Claude Haiku 5.5 and stream to the browser as they are written. Job-fit reports use Claude Sonnet 5.5 with structured output validated by a Pydantic schema, and the system prompts are prompt-cached [project-ask-nitin#3]. An evaluation suite tests factual, negative, off-topic, prompt-injection and job-fit cases, and it fails below a 90% pass rate so it can gate deploys [project-ask-nitin#8].

cases.question: Which AI models does the Ask Nitin assistant use?
cases.answer: The Ask Nitin assistant uses Claude Haiku 5.5 for chat answers, streamed to the browser as they are written [project-ask-nitin#3]. Job-fit reports use Claude Sonnet 5.5, with structured output validated by a Pydantic schema [project-ask-nitin#3]. Model and provider names are set in configuration, so another provider can be tried without changing the rest of the code [project-ask-nitin#2].
